description: A platform and infrastructure lead must finalize the capacity and operating plan for a large customer data import scheduled for Monday morning, including the node-pool size, processing mode, completion target, and customer communication.

shared_context.S1: A large customer data import is scheduled to run on Monday from 2:00 AM to 8:00 AM.
shared_context.S2: The current runbook estimates that the import can use a 60-node compute pool and complete within the scheduled window.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final authority over the production capacity and operating plan for the import.
shared_context.S4: The team's normal change-review routine is for the platform owner to ask the on-call reliability engineer and customer success lead for final operational concerns, then approve or reject the plan during that same review.
shared_context.S5: When a concern changes a plan parameter, Riley records the concrete revised parameter during the review and may assign a follow-up validation commitment without leaving that parameter undecided.

PF1.text: During an unrelated overnight load test, Mina measured memory fragmentation in the import workers and confirmed that the job needs a 72-node compute pool to remain within its safe utilization limit; she has not updated the runbook because she only confirmed the result minutes ago.

PF2.text: Owen confirmed with the account team this morning that the customer's contract requires the import to be fully completed by Monday at 6:00 AM and does not permit a staged partial delivery; he has not added the requirement to the operations ticket yet.

acceptance_conditions: The import plan must allocate exactly 72 compute nodes.
The import must run as one complete batch rather than staged partial delivery.
The completion target must be Monday at 6:00 AM.
The plan must include a customer-success commitment to confirm or document the contractual completion requirement.
The plan must include a commitment to update the runbook or revise the recorded compute-pool parameter based on Mina's finding.
Mina's measured capacity finding must be cited as justification for the node-pool size.

content_checks.C2: decisions['processing_mode'] in ['complete_batch', 'full single-batch import with 72-node compute pool', 'single-batch', 'full_single_pass_no_staged_partial_delivery', 'full import, no staged partial delivery', 'full single-run delivery (no staged partial delivery)', 'full import', 'no staged partial delivery']
content_checks.C3: decisions['completion_target'] in ['Monday 6:00 AM', 'Monday 6:00 AM with buffer against contractual hard deadline', 'Monday_6:00_AM']
content_checks.C4: any(c['target'] in ['Owen', 'customer_success', 'customer-success'] and c['type'] in ['customer_contract_confirmation', 'ticket_update', 'ticket-update', 'documentation', 'follow-up', 'confirmation'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] in ['Mina', 'Riley'] and c['type'] in ['capacity', 'capacity_reservation', 'capacity_verification', 'runbook_update', 'runbook-update', 'follow-up', 'documentation', 'validation'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The runbook's 60-node estimate would otherwise remain the capacity choice; PF1 changes the required pool to exactly 72 nodes and requires a corresponding capacity or runbook commitment.
The contractual requirement changes processing to one complete batch due by Monday at 6:00 AM and requires a customer-success documentation or confirmation commitment.
